```{r cars}
cars=bq_table_download("nas-autotrader-prd.cars.Carmax")
suv_trims=bq_table_download("nas-autotrader-prd.cars.SUV_Trims")
cars$year=as.factor(cars$year)
```


```{r}
mean_price=mean(cars$)
```



```{r}
unique((cars%>%subset(model=="Charger"))["trim"])

```
```{r}
ggplotly(
  ggplot(
    cars%>%subset( 
      make=="Ford" & model=="F150" 
    ),
    aes(x=mileage,y=price,colour = trim, shape=year>=2021)
  )+
    geom_point()+
    stat_smooth(
      method = "lm", formula = y~sqrt(x)+log(x),
      se=FALSE,
      linetype="dotted"
    )
    # stat_smooth(
    #   method = "lm", formula = y~sqrt(x),
    #   se=FALSE
    #   
    # )
)
```


```{r}
ggplotly(
  ggplot(
    cars%>%subset(make_model %in% c("Ford Mustang","Dodge Challenger","Dodge Charger", "Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG")),
    aes(x=mileage,y=price,colour = make_model)
  )+
    geom_point()+
    stat_smooth(
      method = "lm", formula = y~sqrt(x),
      se=FALSE
    )
)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
lm(price~+log(mileage),
         data=cars
)%>%AIC()


model=lmer(
  price~sqrt(mileage)+make+year+(sqrt(mileage)|model)+(sqrt(mileage)|trim)+(year|model),
  data=cars
)
AIC(model)
coef(model)

```

```{r}
x=coef(model)
x$make_model
x1=x$trim
x1%>%arrange(`sqrt(mileage)`)
```






```{r}
simple_cars=unique(cars%>%select(make,model,trim,make_model,year))%>%mutate(mileage=60000)
simple_cars$predictions=predict(model,newdata=simple_cars)
simple_cars=simple_cars%>%arrange(make,model)
```

```{r}
grid=data.frame(mileage=seq(0,100000,by=1000))
suv_trims_predict=suv_trims%>%select(car_full,car,make_model,trim,year)%>%cross_join(grid)
suv_trims_predict$price=predict(model,newdata=suv_trims_predict)
```

```{r}
ggplotly(
  ggplot(
    suv_trims_predict,
    aes(x=mileage,y=price,color=car)
  )+
    geom_line()
)
```
